children: SYDNEY--Australian wages grew at their fastest quarterly pace since late 2023 in the third quarter, adding pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia to consider a further interest-rate rise.
The wage price index rose 1.1% from the previous quarter, and by 3.5% annually, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Wednesday.
The data beat markets expectations for a 1.0% rise over the quarter and follows comments by RBA Gov. Michele Bullock on Tuesday that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.
The RBA has already raised interest rates five times this year, but the central bank remains concerned that domestic demand remains strong, keeping inflation well above target.
While quarterly wage growth showed surprising strength, the annual rate has slowed from a peak of 4.3% in late 2023, the ABS said.
Private sector wages rose 3.4% in annual terms in the quarter, up from 3.2% a year earlier, while public sector wages grew 3.9% in annual terms, up from 3.8% a year earlier.
Wage growth in the public sector has been outpacing the private sector's for nearly two years, the ABS said.
The Fair Work Commission, the country's wages umpire, announced a 4.75% increase to base wages in the middle of the year, which supported private sector wages.
The main driver of public sector wage growth was pay rises for state government front-line workers such as nurses, midwives and police officers, the ABS said.
